problem: Ford needed cash to fund its turnaround and survive losses.
title: Ford borrows about $23 billion against its assets before the financial crisis
context: Ford posted a record loss in 2006 under new CEO Alan Mulally.
decision_made: Raise roughly $23.4 to $24 billion in loans by mortgaging key assets, including factories, subsidiaries and trademarks.
action_taken: Pursued the One Ford plan; reports say lenders took the blue oval logo as collateral.
observed_outcome: Ford withstood more than $30 billion in losses from 2006 to 2008 and, unlike GM and Chrysler, avoided a government bailout and bankruptcy. It reported a profit in 2009.
lessons: Securing a large cash cushion before a downturn can decide whether a company survives it.
limitations: Loan totals differ by source ($23.4 to $24 billion). Some of the supporting articles are retrospectives and opinion pieces, so the link between the loan and avoiding a bailout is partly interpretation.

claims.claim_text: Ford raised almost $24 billion in 2006 by mortgaging key assets.
The cash cushion let Ford stay afloat without a bailout, unlike GM and Chrysler.
